page: Amazon Web Services c6g.2xlarge is an arm64 compute-optimized virtual instance powered by the AWS Nitro System. It is equipped with 8 dedicated physical cores based on the ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 architecture running at 2.5 GHz, without simultaneous multithreading (1 thread per core). Memory is configured at 16.0 GB total, delivering 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance does not include integrated local storage or hardware accelerators, relying on external network-attached volumes for persistent data, and features a baseline network throughput of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark data reflects solid multi-threaded efficiency offset by modest single-core throughput. The instance achieves a Geekbench multi-core score of 5457.0 and a multi-core stress-ng rating of 12132.72, both placing within the middle 50% of tested instances. Clang software compilation also demonstrates solid performance at 8600.0 points. Conversely, single-core metrics fall into lower brackets, marked by a Geekbench single-core score of 960.0 and weak compression rates, including single-threaded gzip at 20.32 GB/sec. Cryptographic performance in PassMark is low (1092.15), despite hardware AES support.

In operational throughput tests, the c6g.2xlarge maintains stable results for memory and web serving workloads, logging 9.39 million Redis SET operations per second and 9.46 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. Natural language model processing is constrained by the lack of specialized vector instructions (such as AVX or AMX) and dedicated GPUs, yielding 40.33 tokens/sec on text generation for a 135M parameter model and 6.77 tokens/sec on a 7B model.

From an architectural standpoint, the ARM-based Graviton2 implementation offers strong resource isolation and cost-effective multi-threaded scaling due to its dedicated single-threaded core design. The primary tradeoff lies in the absence of local NVMe storage and subdued single-thread execution speed. The instance is suited for containerized microservices, distributed CI/CD build agents, static web serving clusters, and batch data processing pipelines optimized for arm64 execution.
description: Amazon Web Services c6g.2xlarge is a compute-optimized arm64 cloud instance operating on the AWS Nitro System. Powered by an 8-core AWS Graviton2 Neoverse-N1 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz with a 1:1 thread-to-core mapping, it is backed by 16.0 GB of system memory and 2 Gbps baseline networking. The instance contains no bundled local storage and no GPU acceleration. Benchmarks show balanced multi-core capability with 5457.0 in Geekbench multi-core and 8600.0 in Clang compilation, alongside consistent operational metrics such as 9.39 million Redis SET operations per second. However, single-core execution and advanced AI inference remain weak due to architectural and instruction set limitations. The instance provides a cost-efficient hardware profile for parallelized arm64 workloads, including web serving, batch processing, and CI/CD pipelines.
